extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in media criticism, public-health misinformation, and contemporary podcast controversies
extracted.subtask_description: Identifying and critiquing harmful practices and behaviors on a popular podcast (misinformation, racist language, sexual coercion humor) and their public-health and reputational consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcasting misinformation, particularly regarding COVID-19
rubrics_metrics.description: Has "a concerning history of broadcasting misinformation, particularly regarding the COVID-19 pandemic."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: episodes featuring Robert Malone and Peter McCullough that floated baseless claims (e.g., mass-formation psychosis, conspiracy theories about misdiagnosed COVID deaths, masks not protecting, asymptomatic spread denial, vaccines causing unreported deaths). Platforms have removed content for violating COVID-19 disinformation policies; measure includes frequency/severity of false claims and whether those claims are presented as factual or challenged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platforming unqualified or discredited guests
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing a large platform to guests who lack relevant qualifications or have a history of spreading falsehoods (e.g., Malone, who did not complete a medical residency; McCullough, fired for spreading COVID conspiracies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider guest credentials and track record: whether guest is a practicing clinician or a discredited figure; whether the host frames their claims as expertise; the reach of the platform (e.g., up to 190 million downloads/month) which amplifies harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to challenge or fact-check dangerous claims on-air
rubrics_metrics.description: The host failed to push back on guests' pandemic conspiracies and in some cases appeared to agree, rather than interrogate or correct falsehoods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate host behavior: did the host ask critical questions, present counter-evidence, or explicitly correct false claims? Anti-patterns include laughing along, endorsing alternative treatments (ivermectin, hydroxychloroquine), or publicly amplifying guests' claims (e.g., retweeting defenses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributing to public distrust of science and harming public health
rubrics_metrics.description: Amplifying anti-vaccination sentiment and misinformation that "stands to be exacerbated by the anti-vaccination sentiment woven into this and other episodes," thereby harming public understanding and stressing medical systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess downstream effects cited by experts: whether medical professionals warn that the content worsens public distrust, exacerbates pandemic strain, or undermines vaccination efforts. Note institutional responses (doctors' open letters) as evidence of public-health concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of racial slurs and dehumanizing racist language
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeatedly saying the N-word and making racially demeaning remarks (examples: joking about a movie theater being 'Planet of the Apes'; saying of a mixed-race guest: 'you get the body of the Black man and then you get the mind of the white man' and 'Black people... have a different brain').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document specific slurs and demeaning tropes; consider frequency, context (joke vs. endorsement), and whether the host acknowledges wrongdoing. Such language is cited as a distinct harm separate from misinformation and grounds for public backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laughing about or normalizing sexual coercion and misogynistic behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Laughing hysterically as a friend described coercing women into giving him blowjobs for stage time, and defending or retweeting defenses of such clips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the host interrogates or condemns abusive accounts versus normalizing/celebrating them (laughing, retweeting defenses, insulting critics). Anti-patterns include treating coercion as punchline or defending participants instead of holding them accountable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public and commercial consequences as indicators of severity
rubrics_metrics.description: Reputational and commercial responses—episodes removed for policy violations, artists removing catalogs from the distributor (Spotify), and public letters from professionals—serve as measures of the seriousness of the host's conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use platform moderation actions (removals), organized boycotts (artists pulling catalogs), and formal complaints (open letters from doctors) as objective signals of harm and community standards being breached.
